stimulus.text: Original secondary passage written for this question. In the late 1400s, Europeans wanted the spices and silks of Asia, but the overland routes to Asia ran through lands ruled by Muslim powers, and after Constantinople fell in 1453 those routes grew costly and uncertain. At the same time, new ships and tools made long ocean voyages possible: the caravel with lateen sails, the compass, the astrolabe, and portolan charts. Portugal sailed down the African coast toward Asia, and Spain, with no route of its own, funded Columbus's voyage west across the Atlantic.

parts.prompt: Identify one economic motive that led Europeans to seek new sea routes to Asia.
Explain how one new ship or tool helped make long ocean voyages possible.
Explain one way the search for sea routes to Asia changed European rivalries.
